newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 a tonne higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open $5 to $10 a tonne higher.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 to $10 higher Friday in line with gains overnight in London, traders said.
"London made its due and a bit better," one trader said.

LIFFE cocoa futures rose in thin trading, bolstered by light shortcovering. The market was expected to open six stg higher and at the midday break benchmark September was up 10 stg at 997 stg aonne, at the top of its 997 to 990 stg range. December was up nine stg at 1,029 stg.

Thursday, New York cocoa futures erased early losses and ended broadly higher. September settled up $19 at $1,516 a tonne after ranging from $1,518 to $1,480. December rose the same to $1,566, while the back months finished $16 to $18 higher.
Technically, traders pegged September resistance at a chart gap between $1,521 and $1,526. Support was put at $1,475, with the next downside target seen at $1,450 to $1,448.
